THIS M.F.A. AND M.F.A. CROB. COMING ON FOR FURTHER HEARING THIS DAY, K.S.MUDAGAL J., DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
Challenging the award in MVC No.339/2012 on the file of MACT and Court of Small Causes,

Bengaluru the Insurer has NC: 2023:KHC:21407 preferred MFA No.3540/2014 and claimants have preferred Cross Objections No.77/2016.
2.
The appellant was respondent No.2 and respondents No.1 to 5 were the claimants, respondent No.6 was respondent No.1 in MVC No.339/2012.
For the purpose of convenience the parties will be referred to henceforth according to their ranks before the Tribunal.
3. Claimant No.1 is the wife, claimant Nos.2 and 3 are the minor children, claimant Nos.4 and 5 are the aged parents of the deceased Krishnakumar.

On 18.03.2008 at 8.30 p.m. when Krishna Kumar was proceeding in his car bearing registration No.KA-03-MD-6178 near Midford garden cross road,
Richmond road, within the limits of Ulsoor Traffic police, the BMTC bus bearing No.KA-01/F-2061 hit the car.
Due to the injuries suffered in the accident Krishnakumar died at the spot.

At the Smt Sheeja Krishnakumar vs The Managing Director on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124724938/
3 relevant time, respondent Nos.1 and 2 were the registered owner and Insurer respectively of the bus bearing No.KA-01/F-2061.
4.

sentences.text: The claimants filed MVC No.339/2012 against the respondents claiming compensation of Rs.1 crore from the respondents on the ground that the accident occurred solely NC: 2023:KHC:21407 due to the actionable negligence of the driver of the bus.
They further contended that they were all depending on the income of the deceased and due to his death they have suffered the damages.
5. Respondent No.1 did not contest the matter.

Respondent No.2/Insurer alone contested the petition denying actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the bus, age, occupation, income of the deceased and its liability to pay the compensation.
It was contended that the accident occurred solely due to the negligence of the deceased himself.
6. In support of case of claimants PWs.1 and 2 were examined and Exs.P1 to P35 were marked.
On behalf of respondent No.2, RWs.1 to 3 were examined and Exs.R.1 to R6 were marked.
7. The Tribunal on hearing the parties by the impugned award held that the accident occurred due to the contributory negligence on the part of the driver of the bus as well as deceased Krishnakumar.
The Tribunal apportioned the negligence at 80% and 20% between the driver of the bus and the deceased.

The Tribunal further held that at the time of the accident, deceased Krishnakumar was earning salary of NC: 2023:KHC:21407 Rs.21,000/- per month, deducted one-third from the same for his personal expenses, added 30% to the same by way of future prospects, considering his age at 42 years, applied 14 multiplier and awarded compensation of Rs.23,52,000/- on the head of loss of dependency.

8. The Tribunal in all awarded the total damages at Rs.34,52,600/- as per the table below:
 Sl. Particulars Compensation  No. awarded in Rs.
 1. Loss of dependency 23,52,000/-
 (21000 X 2/3 X 12 X 14)
 2. Add 30% future prospects 7,05,600/-
 3. Loss of consortium to P1 1,00,000/-

4 . Loss of love and affection 1,00,000/-
 To P2 and 3 Rs.50,000/- each

5. Loss of Love and affection 50,000/-
 To P.4 and 5 Rs.25,000/- each  5. Loss of Estate 1,25,000/-
 To P1 to 5 Rs.25,000/- each  6. Transportation of dead body 20,000/-
 and funeral expenses

Total 34,52,000/-

sentences.text: 9. The Tribunal on deducting 20% towards the contribution of deceased Krishnakumar in the occurrence of the accident, awarded the compensation of Rs.27,62,000/- with interest at 8% p.a.
The Insurer and the claimants both have NC: 2023:KHC:21407 challenged the award on the ground of the negligence as well as quantum of compensation.

10. Sri O Mahesh, learned Counsel appearing for the Insurer reiterating the grounds of the appeal submits that the complaint averments and the evidence of RW.2 shows that the deceased himself was rash and negligent.
Therefore, the Tribunal committed error in holding that the negligence of the deceased was only 20%.

He submits that to show that the deceased was having consistent income of Rs.21,000/-, the bank statement was not produced, therefore, the finding regarding monthly income of the deceased is incorrect.
He further submits that there was no evidence to show that the deceased had vibrant career in future, therefore, awarding of compensation on the head of future prospects is erroneous.
The compensation awarded on the other heads and rate of interest is also on the higher side.

11. Per contra, learned Counsel for the claimants submits that the evidence of PW.2, income tax returns, bank passbook Ex.P29, salary slip Ex.P32 show that the income of the deceased was higher than the one assessed by the Tribunal.

The Police records and the evidence of the witnesses NC:
2023:KHC:21407 show that the accident occurred due to actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the bus alone.
The complainant was not an eye witness.
His statement in the complaint is that he only heard somebody saying that the deceased was negligent which is hearsay.
He submits that, RW.2 himself on investigation filed charge sheet only against the bus driver.
Therefore, his evidence that he learnt that the deceased was also negligent cannot be accepted.
The compensation awarded on all the heads is on the lower side.
Therefore, the appeal shall be dismissed and the cross objections be allowed.

12. On hearing both side and on perusal of the records the points that arise for consideration are:
(i) Whether the finding of the Tribunal that the accident occurred due to contributory negligence of the driver of the bus and deceased Krishnakumar in the ratio of 80%
and 20% is sustainable in law ?
(ii) Whether the compensation awarded is just and fair one?
ANALYSIS Reg. Negligence:
13.
Both side do not dispute the occurrence of the accident on 18.03.2008 at 8.30 p.m. near Richmond road, Bengaluru involving car No.KA 03 MD 6178.

It is not disputed NC:
2023:KHC:21407 that the car was being driven by the deceased and BMTC bus was driven by RW.1.
It is also not disputed that based on the FIR Ex.P1, RW.2 on conducting investigation filed charge sheet as per Ex.P2 against the driver of the bus alone.
Ex.P3 to 5 are the spot mahazar, sketch of scene of occurrence and the inquest report in the case.

RW.2 drawing those documents is also not in Smt Sheeja Krishnakumar vs The Managing Director on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124724938/
5 dispute.

entities.text: Smt Sheeja Krishnakumar vs The Managing Director on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Ex. P1
the complaint was filed by Siddaraju, Asst. Sub-Inspector.
The above documents are the prima facie evidence of the occurrence of the accident due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the bus.
14. Respondents were expected to rebut the above said evidence.
Respondent No.1 the owner of the bus did not contest the petition to deny the actionable negligence on the part of its driver.
Ex . P1
the complaint was filed by one Siddaraju, Asst. Sub-Inspector of Ulsoor Traffic Police Station.
Admittedly he was not eye witness to the incident.
In the complaint he purportedly stated that when he rushed to the spot, people gathered there told him that the car driver overtook another vehicle and came forward.
Thus the said statement was hearsay.
Moreover the complainant was not examined.

- 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:21407 15. RW.2 who files charge sheet after investigation during the course of chief examination admits that in the complaint there is recital about people at the spot talking that the driver of the car had overtaken.
Overtaking of the car assuming so, itself does not amount to rashness and negligence.
Apart from that RW.2 in his chief examination denied the suggestion that driver of the car was overtaking the bus.
He states that the driver of the bus had overtaken.
RW.2 was the witness of respondent No.2 itself.
Therefore, whatever he has stated binds it.
16. RW.2 was not an eye witness.
He submitted charge sheet after recording of the statements of the witnesses, visiting the spot, drawing Ex.P4 the spot mahazar at the scene of offence.
The sketch of scene of offence shows that the bus had crossed the centre point of the road and had over stretched on the right side road.
Ex.P4 shows that the total width of the road was about 20 meters.
The car driver was driving the car at a distance of 8 meters from the left border of the road.
Where as the bus was at a distance of 11 meters from left road margin line.
Therefore, it is clear that the BMTC bus itself has gone on the extreme right side.
The evidence of RW.2 further - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:21407 fortifies the observations in Ex.P4.
Even assuming that the driver of the car had overtaken another vehicle, he was still within his road limits.
The contention of BMTC driver that the car had overtaken and was rash and negligent cannot be accepted.
The Tribunal in fastening 20% contributory negligence to the deceased has acted contrary to the evidence on record more particularly Ex.P4, the charge sheet and the other oral evidence.
Therefore, the finding of the Tribunal warrants interference imputing the entire actionable negligence to the driver of bus itself.

Reg. Quantum:
17.
Claimants contended that the deceased was a law graduate and he was working as Manager Legal in Gina Engineering Co. Ltd and earning Rs.35,000/- per month.

To substantiate their contention Smt Sheeja Krishnakumar vs The Managing Director on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124724938/
6

entities.text: Smt Sheeja Krishnakumar vs The Managing Director on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
with regard to qualification of the deceased they produced Ex.P8 to P15 his SSLC, PUC marks cards,
certificate of English Typewriting senior examination and English Typewriting speed test, degree certificate, law degree certificate and enrolment certificate.
Those documents were not disputed.
To prove that victim was working in Gina Engineering Co. Ltd., they examined PW.2 the senior consultant - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC:21407 of M/s Gina Engineering co. Ltd.
His employment in the said company was not disputed.
18. Though the claimants contended that victim was earning Rs.35,000/- per month, as per their own document Ex.P29 bank pass book his last drawn salary was Rs.26,520/-.
As per the income tax returns Ex.P33 his annual income was Rs.2,50,729/-.
Therefore, that can be taken as annual income.
Out of that 10% has to be deducted towards payment of tax which comes to Rs.25,073/-.

Therefore his income comes to (Rs.2,50,729 - 25,073) Rs.2,25,656/-.
19.
The deceased was working in a private organization.
He was aged 42 years.

As per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi1 25% has to be superadded to the annual income which comes to (Rs.2,25,656x25/100)= Rs.56,414/-.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: His net annual income comes to Rs.2,82,070/- (2,25,656 + 56,414).
The applicable multiplier is 14.
Therefore, total loss of dependency is Rs.39,48,980/- (2,82,070 X 12).
The parents of the deceased were living separately from the deceased and they filed an affidavit saying that they were AIR 2017 SC 5157 - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC:21407 not dependant on their son.
Therefore, the Tribunal rightly deducted one third from the income of the deceased towards his personal expenses.

On such deduction the damages on head of loss of dependency comes to (Rs.39,48,980 x 2/3) Rs.26,32,653.33 rounded off to Rs.26,32,653/-.
20.

As per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pranay sethi's case and Magma General Insurance Company Ltd. v. Nanu Ram2, the claimants being widow, minor children and aged parents of the deceased are entitled to consortium at the rate of Rs.40,000/- each with escalation of 10% which comes to Rs.2,20,000/-.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Ltd. v. Nanu Ram2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On the conventional heads viz., loss of estate and funeral expenses each, the claimants are entitled to Rs.15,000/- with escalation of 10% which comes to Rs.33,000/-.

Therefore the just compensation payable is as follows:
 Sl. Particulars Compensation  No. awarded in Rs.
 1. Loss of dependency 26,32,653/-
 2. Loss of consortium 2,20,000/-
 3. Loss of estate and funeral 33,000/-
 expenses Smt Sheeja Krishnakumar vs The Managing Director on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124724938/
7  Total 28,85,653/-
 2018 (18) SCC 130  - 14 -  NC: 2023:KHC:21407
The Tribunal without assigning any reasons awarded interest at 8% pa.
The claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is not recovery proceedings based on contractual liability.
Therefore, as per Section 171 of the MV Act read with Section 34 of CPC, the claimants are entitled to interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
There was delay of 725 days in filing the cross objection.
If there was no cross objection, the finding with regard to 20% contributory negligence on the part of the deceased would not have been reversed.
Therefore, the claimants are not entitled to interest for 725 days on 20% of the award amount.
For the aforesaid reasons, appeals deserve to be allowed in part.

Hence the following:
ORDER
The appeal and the cross objections are partly allowed.

The impugned award is modified as follows:
i) The claimants are entitled to compensation of Rs.28,85,653/- with interest thereon at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization excluding interest on 20% of the award amount for 725 days.
ii) Respondent Nos.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the award amount.
- 15 - NC: 2023:KHC:21407 iii) Respondent No.2 being the Insurer shall deposit the said amount on adjusting the amount already deposited, if any before the Tribunal within four weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
iv) The award of the Tribunal with regard to apportionment and investment is maintained.

(ii) Whether the compensation awarded is just and fair one?
ANALYSIS Reg. Negligence:
13.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The deceased was working in a private organization.
Therefore, the Tribunal rightly deducted one third from the income of the deceased towards his personal expenses.
The Tribunal without assigning any reasons awarded interest at 8% pa.
The claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is not recovery proceedings based on contractual liability.
Therefore, as per Section 171 of the MV Act read with Section 34 of CPC, the claimants are entitled to interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
If there was no cross objection, the finding with regard to 20% contributory negligence on the part of the deceased would not have been reversed.
opennyai_summary.decision:
There was delay of 725 days in filing the cross objection.
Therefore, the claimants are not entitled to interest for 725 days on 20% of the award amount.
For the aforesaid reasons, appeals deserve to be allowed in part.
Hence the following:
ORDER
The appeal and the cross objections are partly allowed.
The impugned award is modified as follows:
i) The claimants are entitled to compensation of Rs.28,85,653/- with interest thereon at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization excluding interest on 20% of the award amount for 725 days.
ii) Respondent Nos.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the award amount.
- 15 - NC: 2023:KHC:21407 iii) Respondent No.2 being the Insurer shall deposit the said amount on adjusting the amount already deposited, if any before the Tribunal within four weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
iv) The award of the Tribunal with regard to apportionment and investment is maintained.
